topic: Are there scalability limitations when applying the iterative power algorithm to dense multi-beam satellite networks?
consensus_response: The iterative power algorithm exhibits scalability limitations in dense multi-beam satellite networks due to increased computational complexity and interference management challenges. As the number of beams (N) increases, mutual coupling between adjacent elements grows, causing interference and degrading algorithm performance. This compromises capacity maximization and computational resources required, exacerbating scalability limitations. Advanced channel estimation techniques can improve accuracy and reduce latency in estimating CSI, potentially enhancing the performance of iterative power algorithms. However, they also introduce new challenges related to real-time channel estimation and algorithmic modifications.
reference_context: The number of beams per satellite can take any value in {7, 19, 37, 74, 370, 740}, but must be fewer than or equal to 74 for LEO networks due to power limitations. The array factor's mainlobe width is inversely proportional to the number of beams (N) and directly proportional to beam spacing (d). As N increases, d must decrease, leading to increased mutual coupling between adjacent elements.
